tossups.text: He was supposedly praised by a gentleman from Normandy named Lamord, making another character jealous. In his first lines, which come shortly after the departure of Cornelius and Voltimand, he begs leave to return to France. He dismisses the character's favor as "A violet in the youth of primy nature" in taking leave of his sister, then patiently listens to such tidbits as "Be thou familiar, but by no means vulgar" in a lecture by his father which culminates with the advice, "to thine own self be true." For 10 points name this son of Pollonius and brother of Ophelia in Hamlet.

For an ideal gas, this property is proportional to the average kinetic energy of the particles. Relative humidity is computed by comparing the wet-bulb and dry-bulb measurements of this quantity. According to the third law of thermodynamics, a perfect crystal has zero entropy when this property is absolute zero. For 10 points, name this quantity whose SI unit is the kelvin and that can also be measured on the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales.

The lines of two prayers recited during this holiday are arranged according to the aleph-bet, and those prayers are the Ashamnu and Al Chet. The tradition of Kapparot during this holiday involves swinging a chicken over one's head and giving it to the poor, and it is tradition to read the entire Book of Jonah during this holiday. The days leading up to this occasion are known as the Days of Awe, and the Kol Nidre is read on this holiday which takes place on the tenth of Tishrei. For ten points, identify this holiday occurring ten days after Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish "Day of Atonement" during which Jews fast.

The "Green Dogs" militia propped up the regime of this ruler, who unsuccessfully attempted to stamp out his nickname "Mighty Mouth" from his days as a goatherd. Under this dictator, a new alphabet based on the Roman alphabet without the letters p, v, and z was created. This dictator launched a revanchist invasion of his country's western neighbor with Soviet backing, only for the Soviets to immediately switch sides and supply his enemy with 15,000 Cuban mercenaries. Nation-building efforts launched by this dictator included the attempted abolition of the qabil clan system. This "Scientific Socialism" proponent negotiated with Helmut Schmidt to let German special forces retrieve a PFLP-hijacked Lufthansa plane. Over a million refugees fled into his country after his disastrous invasion of the Ogaden region. After his power was sapped by rebels like Mohamed Farah Aidid, he was derisively nicknamed the "Mayor of Mogadishu." For 10 points, name this dictator under whom Somalia devolved into a failed state.

In relativistic situations, it generalizes to the Klein-Gordon or Dirac equations. In general, this equation can be written down by equating the operation of the Hamiltonian on a function with multiplying the function's derivative with respect to time by "i minus h-bar." For a time independent Hamiltonian, solving it completely gives the energy eigenstates allowed in a given system as well as the allowed wave functions. For 10 points, identify this central equation of quantum mechanics named after an Austrian scientist who also had a thought experiment about cats.

The drug rocecoxib contains an atom of this element double-bonded to two different oxygens and is better known by the trade name Vioxx. This element is harvested by forcing steam through the outermost of three concentric pipes and compressed air through the innermost, thus allowing the molten form of this element to rise through the third. The most stable form of this element, which is yielded by the Frasch process, consists of either orthorhombic or monoclinic crystals of eight-atom cyclic molecules. Used to form cross-linked bridges in vulcanization, this element can expand its octet like its neighbor, phosphorus. For 10 points, name this element found directly below oxygen on the periodic table and symbolized S.

The protagonist of this story whistles as he passes a lightning-struck tulip tree due to its connection with the death of Major Andre. This story's protagonist rides the stubborn old horse Gunpowder, lent to him by Hans van Ripper. After the main character of this story disappears, Brom Bones marries the beautiful Katrina van Tassel. A schoolteacher's hat and a smashed pumpkin are found near a bridge at this story's climax. For 10 points, name this short story about Ichabod Crane's encounter with the Headless Horseman, written by Washington Irving.

Characters in this novel attend a "feely" based on Othello titled Three Weeks in a Helicopter. After watching a ceremony in which a boy is whipped while navigating between snakes in Malpais, Lenina meets a character who had been gifted The Complete Works of Shakespeare by Popé. Helmholtz Watson and Bernard Marx are exiled by Mustapha Mond after fighting a group of "alpha" and "beta" clones. John the Savage hangs himself in a lighthouse at the end of, for the 10 points, what dystopian novel about the soma-consuming World State by Aldous Huxley?

A 2011 Science paper produced by the HiRISE project explained how, on Mars, these objects can become destabilized by the sublimation of dry ice. Like yardangs and loess, they are produced via Aeolian processes, which include saltation, surface creep, and suspension. Types of these geologic objects include barkhans and draa, and both "fossilized" ones and those that "move" are found in ergs. "Reversing" ones are formed where seasonal winds blow in different directions. For 10 points, name these large accumulations of sand.

This author wrote of a "spotted hawk" who "complains of" the poet's "gab and his loitering" in one work that declares "I too am untranslatable." That poem by this man begins "I celebrate myself and sing myself" and includes the line "I sound my barbaric yawp over the roofs of the world." This man also wrote a poem about a ship that "weathered every rack" despite the death of its commanding officer; that poem is an elegy for Abraham Lincoln. For 10 points, name this author of "O Captain! My Captain!" who compiled his work in Leaves of Grass.

One of these presentations referenced the overshadowing of the "solitary inventor, tinkering in his shop" by "task forces of scientists in laboratories." That example warned against the "acquisition of unwarranted influence . . . by the military-industrial complex." A recent presenter of one of these said he was leaving the stage "more optimistic about this country than when [he] started." The first of these was actually presented as an open letter and warned against the "baneful effects of the spirit of party," while also announcing that the presenter wouldn't seek a third term. For 10 points, what are these speeches given at the end of the term of an outgoing US chief executive?

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for muscle fatigue. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this contraction-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The contraction is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in muscle fatigue.

tossups.text: This movement led one college student to declare that his people have given, "Blood, sweat and toil" to defend "bureaucratic organs." Roderick McFarquhar argued against the belief that this movement was actually an attempt by one man to identify his enemies, and this movement lead to a speech about 600,000 plows by Li Kouzi. One element of this effort was an attempt to cooperate with the CUF and it was introduced in a speech entitled, "On the Correct Handling of Contradictions Among the People." This campaign was followed quickly by the Anti-Rightist campaign and was led by Zhou Enlai. FTP, name this brief effort by the Chinese Communist Party to encourage a variety of new opinions on various issues.

This province's city of Gatineau [ga-tih-NOH] is part of its National Capital Region. This province forms the majority of the Labrador Peninsula. Its largest city, on an island in the confluence of the Ottawa and St. Lawrence Rivers, hosted the opening ceremonies of the 1976 Summer Olympics in the Stade [stahd] Olympique. For ten points, name this French-speaking Canadian province, home to Montreal.

Georges Lefebvre [LE-FE-VREH] divided this event into "aristocratic," "bourgeois," and "popular" phases in its Marxist interpretation. Mary Wollstonecraft wrote A Vindication of the Rights of Woman in response to this event. Women marched on the royal palace with cannons to protest the price of bread during this event, which included a peasant uprising in the "Great Fear." Abbe Sieyes [AH-BAY SEE-YIZE] wrote What is the Third Estate? during this event. The Bastille was stormed in, for 10 points, what event that led to the execution of Louis XVI [THE 16th]?

In the early 20th century, perennialists like Robert Maynard Hutchins advocated a normative approach to this field, in contrast to the "progressive" theories of this discipline favored by thinkers like Rudolf Steiner. The "banking model" was critiqued by a Brazilian theorist in this field named Paulo Freire. John Dewey emphasized the role of experience in a book whose title pairs this field with Democracy. Horace Mann's reforms in Massachusetts were inspired by innovations made in this field by Maria Montessori. For 10 points, pedagogy is the study of what process by which students acquire knowledge?

The government should not attempt to influence aggregate demand at all, because fiscal policy is ineffective. Instead, the money supply should increase at a steady rate equal to the long-term growth rate of production. The long-term aggregate supply curve is vertical. For 10 points-identify the economic school of thought which promulgates such ideas, championed by Milton Friedman.

In 1844, this modern country's navy appointed as its chief painter a man whose two depictions of the brig Mercury and 1850 masterpiece The Ninth Wave are among his more than three thousand seascapes. An artist from this present-day country who studied under a man known as Theophanes the Greek removed two figures from a work titled The Hospitality of Abraham to create a piece that depicts the Oak of Mamre behind three angels, who sit around a table and bless a cup containing a calf's head. A husband-and-wife pair from this modern country founded Rayonism, which in turn inspired an artist from this country to pioneer geometric abstraction with paintings like Black Circle and White on White, foundational examples of this country's Suprematist movement. For 10 points, name this country home to Natalia Goncharova, Kazimir Malevich, and the icon painter Andrei Rublev.

This person collaborated with James Baldwin on A Rap on Race and noted that females are the dominant figures in the Chambri Lake region in Sex and Temperament in Three Primitive Societies. She interviewed 68 women between the ages of 9 and 20 for another work, and that book, criticized by Derek Freeman, studies the sexual development of adolescents in Polynesia. For 10 points, name this American anthropologist who wrote Coming of Age in Samoa.

This city is home to the Institute for Advanced Study, where Albert Einstein worked after moving to the US. Hugh Mercer was mortally wounded during a Revolutionary War battle over this city that took place a week after Washington surprised the Hessians by crossing the Delaware River. Since 1945, this college town has been its state's governor's residence, rather than the state capital of Trenton. For 10 points, name this town that is home to New Jersey's only Ivy League university.

parts.text: Name this novel about parish priest Charles Primrose, who goes bankrupt, causing Arabella Wilmot's marriage to his son to be called off.
The Vicar of Wakefield was penned by Oliver Goldsmith, who was from this island which was also the home of Seamus Heaney.
Oliver Goldsmith was inspired by this man's Persian Letters to write The Citizen of the World. This man articulated the theory of "the Separation of Powers" in The Spirit of the Laws.

bonuses.leadin: The main family finds out Mr. Burchell is in fact Sir William Thornhill near this end of this novel, and William eventually marries that family's daughter Sophia. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these surface imprints left by friction ridges on the epidermis. Immigrants and infants have to register theirs so that forensics agencies can uniquely identify a suspect at a crime scene.
This fingerprint pattern can be classified as radial or ulnar, and consists of ridges making a backward turn without twist.
This other fingerprint pattern can be either single-cored or double-cored, and its ridges make a complete circuit.

bonuses.leadin: Scotland Yard was the first bureau to establish an agency for studying these identifying marks. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this monotheistic religion that was founded by Nanak and which celebrates ten gurus.
Uncut hair and the carrying of a sword are among this number of "K" s in Sikhism. There are also this many Thieves, or vices, in Sikhism.
This eleventh and eternal "Guru of the Sikhs" is divided by ragas, or musical settings into 1430 pages of religious text.

bonuses.leadin: The Vaisakhi harvest festival is the most sacred in this religion. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this fictional event from a novel in which Liu Bei, Guan Yu, and Zhang Fei promise to band together and protect the Han Empire from Yellow Turban rebels? It is named for the tranquil location where the vow takes place.
acceptableAnswers: The Oath of the Peach Garden

parts.text: The Oath of the Peach Garden is an event from a classical Chinese novel titled for the "romance" of how many Chinese kingdoms?

This real-life battle is heavily fictionalized in the novel, which features such incidents as Zhuge Liang pretending to use magic to control the eastern wind in order to protect the fire ships and a later sequence in which Guan Yu spares this battle's loser, Cao Cao.

bonuses.leadin: During this event, three men profess their hope that they will die on the same day, in the same month, and in the same year. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Atomic nuclei were shown to be tiny masses at the center of atoms in an experiment in which students of Ernest Rutherford fired alpha particles at a thin foil of this precious metal.

Just like electrons, nuclear protons and neutrons are organized into shells. Those shells arise because, as identical fermions, protons and neutrons are subject to this rule that restricts their possible quantum states.
The residual strong force that binds nuclei together is mediated by this set of three very light mesons. Predicted by Hideki Yukawa, these particles were discovered in 1947 by Cecil Powell.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each-identify the following about our understanding of atomic nuclei:

parts.text: Name this molecule whose CCA 3-prime end undergoes aminoacylation to carry amino acids to ribosomes.
The middle arm of tRNA contains three nucleotides given this name, which bonds to an oppositely named site on messenger RNA that specifies amino acids.
These proteins, one of which in prokaryotes is known as "thermo unstable," aid translation by forming complexes with tRNA at the ribosome's T site.

bonuses.leadin: The "cloverleaf structure" of this molecule contains a D-loop and an acceptor stem. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this novel by Miguel de Cervantes about the adventures of a delusional "knight," his horse Rocinante, and his squire Sancho Panza.
Don Quixote accidentally tries to fight these things during one of his adventures, which he mistakenly believes to be giants.
Many of Don Quixote's delusions come from stories of this knight "of Gaul."

bonuses.leadin: In one scene in this novel, the protagonist believes his brains are melting when he puts on a helmet filled with cheese curds. For 10 points each:

parts.text: That fictional dish is the longest word in this language, which was used by playwrights in Ancient Athens to write comedies and tragedies.
The dish appears in The Assemblywomen, a play by this Ancient Greek playwright who also wrote Lysistrata and depicted The Thinkery in his play The Clouds.
The Clouds was a play in the "Old" form of this genre, which Aristophanes pioneered. Shakespeare wrote many plays in this humorous genre, which were contrasted with histories and tragedies.

bonuses.leadin: In one play in this language, a stew with a 173-letter-long name is served. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these circuit components, which store energy in the form of charge. Their strength is measured in farads.
Capacitors consist of two parallel plates surrounding these insulating materials that are used to increase capacitance. Their namesake "constant" is symbolized lowercase kappa.
Capacitors are an integral part of this type of circuit, whose overall stored energy oscillates in a harmonious manner between an electric and a magnetic field.

bonuses.leadin: The energy in these components is equal to ½ times Q times delta V. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this poem, set in the "bleak December," that begins with the speaker lamenting the loss of his beloved Lenore.
This American wrote "The Raven" and also expanded on the theme of lost love in "Annabel Lee."
In "The Raven," the title bird can only say this word.

bonuses.leadin: This poem's title figure sits upon a bust of Pallas and is told to "take thy beak from out my heart and take thy form from off my door." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this emperor whose subjects beat up some enemies during La Noche Triste after his capture.
Montezuma II was a ruler of this Mexican empire conquered by Hernán Cortés.
The Aztec empire began as this confederation of cities formed against the Tepanecs. It shares its name with the victors and namesakes of a war that destroyed much of Paraguay's adult male population.

bonuses.leadin: This ruler's nephew, Cuauhtémoc, was the last ruler of his polity. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with mouth and salivary glands.
What is the main function of the esophagus in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to mouth and salivary glands.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: Name this document that was replaced in 1947 and signed by a namesake emperor.
The Meiji Constitution was awesome for this guy who got to be the first prime minister in Japanese history. This guy organized a convention with Li that couldn't prevent the Sino-Japanese War.
Much like Ito, this liberal early Japanese prime minister fought the conservative genro. This two-time PM was the lead Japanese representative at the Versailles Conference.

bonuses.leadin: A House of Peers was established by this document that also established the Diet. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This dog is the mascot of the United States Marine Corps and was initially bred for use in a certain kind of "baiting," although this medium-sized dog is now known as a gentle family pet.
This large dog on short legs is well known for its uniquely long ears. Its name comes from the French word meaning "low set" and was a popular French hunting dog.
This smallest dog breed, first discovered in Mexico, cannot exceed 6 pounds and may have descended from the fennec fox.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, name these dog breeds recognized by the American Kennel Club.

parts.text: It starts parallel to the Yangtze River on the Tibetan Plateau and flows south. It then continues through Laos and Cambodia until it cuts across Vietnam and has a delta at Ho Chi Minh City.
acceptableAnswers: Meigong He and Song Me Kong

parts.text: This river forms in Tibet before flowing west across Kashmir and Jammu, and then flows south and becomes the major river of Pakistan. Its valley was the home to many early civilizations.
This river also starts in Tibet, and eventually causes a lot of flooding in Bangladesh during monsoon season, especially in the area where it shares a delta with the Ganges.

bonuses.leadin: There are many large rivers that start out in China or on the Chinese border, but are better known for being elsewhere. Name some of them, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this discipline whose members may conduct ethnography through participant observation. Its other practitioners include Franz Boas and Margaret Mead.
Chagnon called this other "Dangerous Tribe" the "Fierce People" and depicted them as engaging in constant violence. Critics accused Chagnon of causing a measles outbreak among these Amazonian people.

Chagnon's ethnographic film The Ax Fight was criticized for its inauthenticity for providing weapons to its subjects, like this early Robert Flaherty docufiction film that includes a staged walrus hunt.

bonuses.leadin: The subtitle of Napoleon Chagnon's ("SHAG-non's") memoir about his turbulent time in this discipline calls it one of "Two Dangerous Tribes." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these sounds denoted in English by the letters "a," "e," "i," "o," and "u."
This principle of linguistics relates the Indo-European to Germanic transition of voiced stops to voiceless stops and voiceless stops to voiceless fricatives.
Appearing in "free" and "bound" types, these linguistic components are the smallest units of speech with semantic meaning.

bonuses.leadin: A "great shift" of these originating in London occurred in the English language. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Russian stringed instrument with a triangular body. It usually contains three strings, two of them tuned to the same note and a third tuned a fourth higher.

The balalaika appears in Maurice Jarre's Oscar-winning soundtrack for this 1965 David Lean film. The song "Somewhere, My Love" is based on the leitmotif "Lara's theme" from this film, based on a Boris Pasternak novel.
A balalaika orchestra typically contains the round-bodied domra and this other zither-like stringed instrument. Alexander Borodin used a harp to imitate this instrument in his second symphony.

bonuses.leadin: Vasily Andreyev developed the standardized version of this instrument in the 1880s. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Describe this action, the focus of Stanley Milgram's obedience experiment. In that experiment, subjects were instructed to do this to "learners" who failed at a word-memorization task, and generally did so despite being told that it could be extremely painful.
acceptableAnswers: similar answers by asking “in what manner?”

parts.text: Milgram was inspired to conduct the experiment to determine whether the millions of people involved in perpetrating this atrocity could have been merely "following orders". During this event, over six million Jews were killed and millions more forced to flee Europe.

This German-American Jewish philosopher also explored the motivations of Holocaust perpetrators, coining the phrase "the banality of evil" to explain it. She also wrote the books Eichmann in Jerusalem and The Origins of Totalitarianism.

bonuses.leadin: During a study at Yale University, subjects demonstrated an unexpected willingness to take this action. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this type of war in which two or more people claim to be the inheritor of a monarch without an heir.

This country's namesake war of succession was caused by the fear that a union between France and this country would upset the balance of power. Although Philip V from France became its king, balance was kept in Europe.
One side in this war of succession challenged the legitimacy of Maria Theresa's accession to the Habsburg throne.

bonuses.leadin: One of these conflicts involved the children of Margaret II, Countess of Flanders disputing the inheritance of her counties. For 10 points each:
